doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: A flexible woodwind section with alto flutes and contrabass clarinet
summary: Mandel explains his six-woodwind setup of two flutes, two alto flutes, bass clarinet and contrabass clarinet for flexibility.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: One of your characteristic woodwind voicing’s that to my ears is characteristic anyway is, having six reeds and having what sounds like two flutes, two alto flutes, bass clarinet and contrabass clarinet, like you used when I went down to see you do that Kevin Kline end title a couple weeks ago.
That sound is something that I've heard you use before say with Shirley Horn. Say on the Shirley Horn album I think you use something similar right?
Yeah, I’ll talk about that to you a little bit later.

So, Johnny when we broke we were talking about just – we were into a little technical discussion about your woodwind voicing’s and when I went to that film that you did in town about two or three weeks ago with Kevin Kline, I noticed with looking at the score you had six woodwinds and you had two flutes, two alto flutes, bass clarinet and contrabass clarinet and it reminded me of some things I’d heard you do earlier, for among other people, Shirley Horn.

The reason I used that kind of a voicing was basically to give the greatest amount of flexibility. For instance, if I wanted to get a clarinet trio down on the bottom I could break the clarinet loose and have him playing with the bass clarinet, and the contrabass clarinet. And by the same token I had four flutes apart – three flutes apart from that and… well no, wait seven woodwinds.
No you had six right? Two flutes…
Two flutes, two alto flutes, bass clarinet, contrabass clarinet.

Oh, oh, okay, yeah, in an instrumentation like that the bottom alto flute would swing to clarinet if necessary. The top alto flute would swing to flute if necessary, depends on how high or low everything was written and if I wanted to I could move the bass clarinet up to clarinet or if I wanted to get a five flute thing you could do that too. I’d get somebody on – that’s the swing chair that bass clarinet chair, the contrabass clarinet just stayed with what he had. That was really the bottom, unless I got into something where I wanted six-way-stuff you know, then I’d break all six loose from the clarinets.
